commitments.text: As a minimum the access road will be designed, constructed, and maintained to the standards of the Forest Practices Code's Guidebook for Road Engineering.

Regular inspection by an environmental monitor. The District will require year-round access to the well field site following construction for regular maintenance and inspection, and will maintain the road.
At both sites, no clearing between April 15th and July 31st (nesting period) unless approved by an environmental monitor after nest survey.

The proposed well site is adjacent to the Alava Spring Water Company's pipeline right of way. The District will ensure that development of the well site does not have any impact on the existing pipeline.
The District would be pleased to cooperate with all adjacent property and tenure holders regarding this project.

The District of Squamish recognizes the importance of the views of the Squamish Nation regarding the proposed works and is willing to provide additional data that may be required, to answer any questions that result and to take all reasonable steps necessary to address issues identified by this First Nations community.

MOELP have asked for a Well Protection Plan to be prepared. The District agrees the plan is required and it will be undertaken during the detailed design stage of the project. The plan is required in order to ensure that water quality and thus public health are protected.
MOELP have asked that land use in the vicinity of the Mamquam site be addressed and an inventory of potential contamination sources be prepared.

1. The District must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed and operated in 
accordance with the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate.

3. Subject to Condition 1, the District must fulfil all commitments and proposed mitigation measures 
as documented in the Application, including commitments and measures contained in 
supplementary documents and correspondence listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, and must 
comply with all of the Conditions of this Certificate to the reasonable satisfaction of the Minister.

4. Despite Condition 1, if prior to the commissioning of each well field site, the District of Squamish 
proposes a change to the design, location construction or operation of the Project at that well field 
site as described in the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, and despite that the 
change is not a project modification subject to the provisions of the Environmental Assessment 
Reviewable Projects Regulation (B.C. Reg. 276/95), the District of Squamish must provide the 
Executive Director:
a) notice of the proposed change; and
b) plans, analyses, records and other information necessary for an effective assessment by the 
Executive Director of the proposed change.
7.(a) The District must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, have substantially started the Project commencing its construction within five years of the issue date of this Certificate.

7.(b) Within two months of commissioning each well field site, the District must report to the Executive Director on compliance with the Conditions of this Certificate as they relate to each well field site, indicating the mechanisms used to ensure the work was conducted in compliance with the commitment to undertake the Project in general conformity with all technical recommendations prepared by the District's consultants.

10. The District of Squamish must comply with all applicable orders, directions and conditions, and obtain and comply with all applicable tenures, licences, regulations, approvals, standards and permits, or other authorities, which may include or result from the following provincial enactments: a) Health Act; b) Water Act; c) Forest Act; and d) Land Act.
